# Algorithms and latency

Scope: this section covers how the two-plane memory is trained and run, what each step costs, and what to make faster first. Every number marked **[M]** was measured on this cloud container: one x86 thread (Intel Xeon, Sapphire-Rapids class, 2.1 GHz, AVX-512/AMX, a shared host), in Python with NumPy/OpenBLAS and PyTorch eager. **[E]** means an external number I did not verify. **[X]** means my own extrapolation, also unverified. The container has no GPU and no Apple hardware, so every iPhone, Mac and GPU figure is [E] or [X].

Scripts are in `/tmp/claude-0/algos/bench/` (`b1`–`b7`, `common.py`, `bm25lib.py`). Raw results are in `/tmp/claude-0/algos/bench/results/*.json`, and the full table is in `/tmp/claude-0/algos/bench/results/raw_table.txt` (appendix).

**Three measured findings change the design:**
1. The encoder is at least 95% of a memory hop. One short ask takes 26 ms out of 25–36 ms per hop [M].
2. A pyramid beam descent over **untrained** (mean-pooled) parents is fast but loses most of the exact top-10. B=8 keeps 0.52–0.56 of it on a k-means tree [M]. Below about 1e5 leaves, exact leaf scoring is cheap, so the pyramid should set granularity (gist vs leaf) and should not prune until trained parents pass a fidelity gate.
3. Next to the reasoning plane, the memory plane is negligible. It takes milliseconds, while LLM time to first token is 0.35 s to over 10 s [E]. The latency budget is set by how many LLM-driven hops we allow, not by the memory engine.

## Notation

| symbol | meaning |
|---|---|
| $E(\cdot)$ | frozen encoder (bge-small-en-v1.5, 384-d, unit norm); $e_v = E(\text{text}_v)$ is cached per node |
| $S, A$ | state and action bridge heads, $I + UV^\top$ with rank $r=16$ |
| $\hat s = \mathrm{unit}(S\,x)$ | reasoning state (ask, thought, or LLM hidden state in stage 3) |
| $k_v = \mathrm{unit}(A\,e_v)$, $k_v^0$ | cached action key of node $v$; $k_v^0$ is the key as of the last nightly re-key (anchor) |
| $\ell_v(\hat s) = \tau\,\hat s^\top k_v$ | read score, with $\tau = e^{\log 20}$ learned |
| $P_\theta$ | internode encoder (shared-weight attention pooling) |
| $p_v$ | parent state; $g_v$ is its gist text; $t_v = E(g_v)$ |
| $\pi_\text{stop}$, $W$ | stop bridge, write (placement) bridge |
| $O, C$ | nodes opened (shown to R) and nodes cited by R for one ask |

$$\hat s = \mathrm{unit}\big((I+U_SV_S^\top)x\big),\qquad k_v=\mathrm{unit}\big((I+U_AV_A^\top)e_v\big),\qquad \ell_v(\hat s)=\tau\,\hat s^\top k_v$$

$$\alpha_i=\operatorname{softmax}_i\Big(\tfrac{(q_0+W_q\bar c)^\top W_k c_i}{\sqrt d}\Big),\qquad p_v=\mathrm{unit}\Big(W_o\textstyle\sum_i\alpha_iW_vc_i+\bar c+e_{\mathrm{lvl}(v)}\Big)$$

$$\pi_\text{stop}(v)=\sigma\big(w^\top[\ell_v,\ \ell_v-\ell^{\max}_\text{leaf},\ \mathrm{lvl}(v),\ \text{tokens left}]+b\big),\qquad h_v=H\big(\mathrm{id}_v\,\|\,\mathrm{ver}_v\,\|\,h_{c_1}\|\cdots\|h_{c_m}\big)$$

## 1. Training algorithms

Losses used throughout. These are multi-positive InfoNCE in both directions, as in CLM and the current `e5_bridges.py`:

$$\mathcal L_{\to}=-\frac{1}{|Q|}\sum_{q}\frac{1}{|P_q|}\sum_{v\in P_q}\log\frac{e^{\ell_v(s_q)}}{\sum_{u\in\mathcal C_q}e^{\ell_u(s_q)}}\qquad
\mathcal L_{\leftarrow}=-\frac{1}{|V^+|}\sum_{v\in V^+}\frac{1}{|Q_v|}\sum_{q\in Q_v}\log\frac{e^{\ell_v(s_q)}}{\sum_{q'\in Q}e^{\ell_v(s_{q'})}}$$

$$\mathcal R=\|U_SV_S^\top\|_F^2+\|U_AV_A^\top\|_F^2\quad(=\|W-I\|_F^2)$$

### (a) Offline bridge pretraining (public and synthetic data only)

```text
ALGORITHM A  PRETRAIN-BRIDGES
Data: haystacks H = (leaves L_H, asks Q_H, evidence P_q ⊆ L_H). Sources: LoCoMo folds, public multi-session dialogue
      sets with generated questions (check each licence), and synthetic persona histories written offline by an LLM
      with evidence ids. LongMemEval-S stays a held-out test set (as in E7). No Tessera data.
 1  cache e_v = E(text_v) for every leaf and x_q = E(q) for every ask (encoder frozen: done once, ~21 ms/leaf
    fp32 or ~7 ms/leaf bf16 single-thread here [M])
 2  init U_S = U_A = 0, V_S, V_A ~ N(0, 0.01^2), log tau = log 20        # heads start at identity = frozen cosine
 3  split by haystack, never inside one: train / dev (10%) / test (benchmarks, evaluated once at the end)
 4  hardneg[q] <- {} for all q
 5  for epoch = 1 .. 40:
 6      shuffle haystacks; batch = 1..4 haystacks
 7      for each batch:
 8          s_q <- unit(S x_q);  k_v <- unit(A e_v)
 9          C_q <- all nodes of q's own haystack                       # in-haystack negatives (E5 style)
10                 ∪ 256 random nodes of the other haystacks in batch  # easy negatives
11                 ∪ hardneg[q]
12          loss <- L_fwd + L_bwd + 0.01 R ; also L_write and L_stop (below)
13          AdamW step (lr 1e-3, no weight decay; R is the regulariser)
14      every 5 epochs: MINE-HARD-NEGATIVES
15      dev <- recall@10 of RRF(bridged, BM25) on dev haystacks
16      if dev improved: keep theta*; patience <- 0 else patience += 1; if patience = 5: stop
17  return theta* (3 seeds; report the mean and a bootstrap CI on test)

MINE-HARD-NEGATIVES
 1  for each ask q: cand <- top-20 by s_q·k_v in its haystack ∪ top-10 by BM25(q)
 2      remove v ∈ P_q
 3      remove v with cos(e_v, e_p) > 0.95 for some p ∈ P_q          # near-duplicate: probably a false negative
 4      remove v within ±1 turn of any evidence turn; remove v whose text contains the gold answer string
 5      hardneg[q] <- best 10 survivors

Write head (placement), same loop: for each leaf v with true parent π(v) in the training pyramid,
  L_write = -log softmax_u( tau · unit(W e_v) · p_u ) over the parents u at that level of the haystack.
Stop head, same loop, on teacher-forced descents: at each visited node v, label y = 1 if its subtree holds no gold
  evidence not already in context (or an offline LLM judge says the gist alone answers); L_stop = BCE(pi_stop(v), y).
```

Measured cost: one E5 fold (8 LoCoMo chats, about 4.7k nodes, 40 epochs, r=16) took **2.7 s** on one thread [M]. Pretraining is cheap; the scarce input is labelled data.

### (b) Internode encoder, trained jointly with level-wise contrastive losses

$$\mathcal L_\text{tree}=\sum_{\ell=0}^{L}\lambda_\ell\,\mathcal L^{(\ell)}_{\to}\;+\;\mu\sum_{v}\big(1-p_v^\top t_v\big)\;+\;\nu\,\mathcal L_\text{child}\;+\;\lambda\mathcal R,
\qquad
\mathcal L_\text{child}=-\sum_v\frac{1}{|ch(v)|}\sum_{c\in ch(v)}\log\frac{e^{\tau p_v^\top k_c}}{\sum_{c'\in ch(v)\cup ch(\mathrm{sib}(v))}e^{\tau p_v^\top k_{c'}}}$$

In $\mathcal L^{(\ell)}_{\to}$, the positives of ask $q$ are the level-$\ell$ ancestors of its evidence, and the candidates are all level-$\ell$ nodes of the haystack. The gist term ties $p_v$ to the embedding of its written gist. That keeps parent states readable, and $t_v$ becomes the fallback whenever $p_v$ is stale.

```text
ALGORITHM B  TRAIN-PYRAMID (starts from theta_A)
 1  build each training haystack's pyramid with the shipping grouping rule
    (leaves -> sessions / time windows -> topic groups -> root; fan-out <= 16)
 2  once, offline: g_v <- LLM gist of each parent (public/synthetic data only); t_v <- E(g_v)
 3  init P_theta with W_o = 0, so p_v = unit(mean(children) + e_lvl): training starts from mean pooling
 4  phase 1 (2 epochs): heads frozen, train P_theta only
 5  phase 2: joint; head learning rate x0.1
 6  for each epoch, for each haystack batch:
 7      bottom-up for level 1..L: p_v <- P_theta({k_c : c ∈ children(v)}, lvl)       # differentiable;
                                                                                      # ~40 parents per 600-leaf chat
 8      loss <- L_tree (all levels at once) ; step
 9  dev metrics each epoch:
      (i)  recall@10 per level, and leaf recall of the full READ path (must not fall below stage A)
      (ii) descent fidelity F_B = |top10(beam-B descent) ∩ top10(flat)| / 10 at the shipping beam B
10  early stop on (ii) subject to (i); ship only when F_B >= 0.95, otherwise READ keeps flat leaf scoring
```

Why the fidelity gate exists [M, `b3k_kmeans_tree.py`]: leaf-shaped keys, real LoCoMo asks, and a balanced k-means tree whose parents are the mean of their children. Beam descent keeps this share of the exact top-10:

| beam B | 1 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| N = 4096 (depth 3) | 0.15 | 0.40 | 0.56 | 0.71 | 0.84 | 0.94 |
| N = 65536 (depth 4) | 0.16 | 0.39 | 0.52 | 0.64 | 0.76 | 0.85 |

A tree generated to match the geometry gives 0.98–1.00 at every B (best case). A random grouping gives 0.00–0.24 (worst case). Real session or time grouping will fall somewhere in this range, and making it close to 1 is the job of $\mathcal L_\text{tree}$.

### (c) Per-ask online update, with cite filtering

$$k_v\leftarrow\mathrm{unit}\big(k_v+\eta(\hat s-k_v)\big),\qquad\text{if }\|k_v-k_v^0\|>c:\ k_v\leftarrow\mathrm{unit}\Big(k_v^0+c\,\tfrac{k_v-k_v^0}{\|k_v-k_v^0\|}\Big),\quad\eta=0.1,\ c=0.3$$

```text
ALGORITHM C  ONLINE-UPDATE(ask q, state s, opened O, cited C, outcome)        # after the answer, off the critical path
 1  if outcome ∈ {regenerated, thumbs-down, verifier failed, answer withdrawn}: log only; return
 2  C' <- C ∩ O                                   # a node that was never shown cannot be a real cite
 3  C' <- leaves of C'                            # citing a gist credits no leaf; parents are derived state
 4  keep v ∈ C' only if  s·k_v >= 0.2  or  rank_BM25(v | q) <= 10   # at least one independent signal agrees
 5  C' <- the 3 best of C' by s·k_v                # cap per ask
 6  for v ∈ C': anchored move (formula above); mark the ancestors' cached child K/V dirty
 7  append (time, hash(q), s, O, C, C', outcome, head/encoder versions) to the local learning log
 8  never: update heads online; learn from the system's own top hit without a cite (self-loop)
```

Evidence for the filter (E6 and fix-cite-noise, LoCoMo held-out, recall@10 relative to the rank-16 baseline 0.657): the move rule with clean cites gives **+0.020 [0.014, 0.027]**. With 30% wrong cites it gives −0.003, with 60% wrong cites −0.023, and with the self-loop −0.023. The alias rule was strongly negative. Cost: **0.034 ms** per answer [M].

### (d) Nightly consolidation

$$\theta^\star=\arg\min_\theta\ \mathcal L_\text{log}(\theta;T_\text{fit})+\gamma\,\mathcal L_{\to}(\theta;G)+\beta\|\theta-\theta_\text{ship}\|_2^2
\qquad
\text{accept}\iff \mathrm{CI}^{95}_\text{low}\big(\Delta R@10\ \text{on}\ T_\text{eval}\big)\ge-\varepsilon\ \wedge\ \Delta R@10_G\ge-\varepsilon,\ \ \varepsilon=0.005$$

```text
ALGORITHM D  CONSOLIDATE   (iOS BGProcessingTask: charging + idle; resumable; hard budget e.g. 10 min)
 1  snapshot memory version V_t (copy-on-write); apply pending forgets to the log first
 2  triples T = {(s, C', O \ C', time)}; time split: T_fit = oldest 80%, T_eval = newest 20%
    G = bundled public guard set (~2k LoCoMo-style pairs shipped in the app; no user data)
 3  REFIT: theta <- theta_cur; positives C', hard negatives O \ C' (weight 0.5: "not cited" != "irrelevant"),
           1024 sampled negatives, in-batch negatives, CLM backward term; L2-SP pull to theta_ship;
           <= 5 epochs, early stop on T_eval                              # ~8-12 s for 1e4 asks x 5 epochs [M]
 4  GATE (formula above, bootstrap over asks). Reject -> keep theta_cur and skip 5-6
 5  RE-KEY: k_v^0 <- unit(A_theta* e_v); k_v <- k_v^0 + drift_v (keep the online drift only if replay says it helps)
                                                                          # 14 ms / 1e4 keys, 0.3 s / 1e5 [M]
 6  PARENTS: if P_theta changed -> recompute the whole tree bottom-up, else only nodes whose Merkle hash changed
                                                                          # whole tree 64 ms / 1e4, 0.8 s / 1e5 [M]
 7  GISTS: stale = {v : h_v != h_v^gist}; priority = reads(v) x ||p_v - t_v||; re-distil the top G with the
           on-device model; t_v <- E(g_v)                                 # ~2.3 s per gist on iPhone 15 Pro [derived from E]
 8  STRUCTURE: bridges propose
      split v    if fan-out > 16 or 2-means over children's keys gains > kappa
      merge u,w  if p_u·p_w > rho and |u| + |w| <= 16
      move leaf  if the write head prefers another parent by margin > m
      link u<->w if co-cited >= t times in T, or they share an entity
    for proposals in order of predicted gain (cap per night):
      apply to a shadow copy -> recompute affected parents -> replay T_eval through the full READ path
      accept iff recall@10 and descent fidelity do not drop (same gate as step 4)
 9  COMPACT: drop log entries past retention; refresh BM25 statistics (avgdl); rebuild the ANN index if one is used
10  commit V_{t+1} atomically (weights, keys, tree, gists, hashes); keep V_t for one-step rollback
```

### (e) Stage 3: joint loop with an open LLM (research; cloud GPU; public and synthetic data)

$$\mathcal L=\mathcal L_\text{LM}+\alpha_r\sum_h\mathcal L^{(h)}_{\to}+\alpha_s\,\mathcal L_\text{stop}+\alpha_c\,\mathcal L_\text{cite}+\beta\|\phi_\text{heads}-\phi_B\|^2$$

```text
ALGORITHM E  JOINT-OPEN-LLM
Model: Qwen3-8B f + LoRA (r = 16 on q,k,v,o); P_out: hidden state at a <read> token (R^4096) -> R^384 query;
       P_in: node state (R^384) -> 1-4 soft tokens (R^4096); heads S (on P_out), A, stop, write; internode P_theta
 1  init: LoRA = 0; P_out regressed onto E(thought text) from cached pairs (starts in the encoder's space);
    heads and P_theta from B
 2  for round = 1..R:
 3    PHASE 1  parameters (structure frozen)
 4      sample an episode (haystack, question, gold evidence, gold answer)
 5      roll out READ-AGAIN: at hop h, f emits <read>; s_h <- P_out(h_read); READ with teacher forcing
        (missed gold injected with probability p_tf, decayed toward 0)
 6      loss L above: per-decision supervised losses as in CLM; optional REINFORCE on stop with reward
        = correct - lambda * hops
 7      update {LoRA, P_in, P_out, S, A, stop, write, P_theta}; refresh cached keys of the batch's haystacks,
        refresh all keys every K steps
 8    PHASE 2  structure (parameters frozen): re-key, rebuild parents, re-distil stale gists with f,
              structural ops through the D.8 gate on dev
 9    dev: answer accuracy, evidence recall@10, hops per answer, decision latency; early stop
10  deployment: heads trained on f's hidden states do not transfer to Claude or the Apple model; keep the
    encoder-based head set for those, and ship the f-based set only where f runs (Mac / GPU)
```

## 2. Inference algorithms

$$\mathrm{rrf}(d)=\sum_{r\in\{\text{dense},\,\text{lex}\}}\frac{1}{60+\mathrm{rank}_r(d)}$$

### (a) Read path

```text
ALGORITHM R  READ(state_text | hidden state h, ask tokens, K = 10, B = 8, N_flat = 1e5..2.5e5)
 1  s <- unit(S E(state_text))          (stage 3: s <- P_out(h))          # encoder 26 ms here [M]; head 6 us [M]
 2  UPPER LEVELS (only ~N/15 parents: score them all exactly)
      for level 1..L-1: scores_l <- K_l s                                 # 0.05-0.35 ms for 4k-65k leaves [M]
      beam: B best at level 1; at each lower level keep the B best children of the beam;
            optionally add lateral-link neighbours of beam nodes
      for v in beam: if pi_stop(v) > theta_stop: emit v as a GIST item (granularity choice) and do not descend
 3  LEAVES
      if N <= N_flat or F_B < 0.95 (untrained parents):
          dense <- top-50 over ALL live leaves (int8 scan + fp32 re-rank of the top 100)
                                                                          # 0.72 ms fp32 at 1e4; 1.9 ms int8 at 1e5 [M]
      else:
          dense <- top-50 over children(beam) ∪ HNSW(s, ef = 128)         # 0.41 ms at 1e6 [M]
 4  lex <- BM25 top-50 for the ask's tokens (postings / SQLite FTS5)      # 0.04 ms at 1e4, 0.34 ms at 1e5 [M]
 5  fused <- top-K of rrf(dense, lex)  (fuse top-50 lists only)           # 0.024 ms [M]
 6  ctx <- [(node id, level, text or gist, time, parent id) for v in fused ∪ emitted gists], token budget enforced
 7  log O = ids(ctx) for ONLINE-UPDATE; R must cite node ids from ctx
 8  return ctx
```

### (b) Read-again loop (multi-hop)

```text
ALGORITHM RA  READ-AGAIN(ask, H_max = 3, mode ∈ {memory-only, llm-driven})
 1  state <- ask; seen <- {}; ctx_all <- []
 2  for h = 1..H_max:
 3      ctx <- READ(state) minus seen;  if ctx is empty: break
 4      seen ∪= ids(ctx); ctx_all += ctx
 5      if mode = llm-driven:
            thought <- R(ask, ctx_all, "what is still missing?")         # one LLM call per hop
            if thought = ANSWER: break
            state <- thought
        else:
            state <- ask ⊕ the two best new snippets                      # re-encode: 42-71 ms at 64-128 tokens [M]
            if pi_stop(global features of ctx_all) > theta: break
 6      if token budget of ctx_all is exhausted: break
 7  return ctx_all   (hop 1 always runs before or alongside the first LLM request)
```

Measured memory-only loop: 1 / 2 / 3 hops = **25–27 / 76–84 / 138–143 ms** median (p95 up to 209 ms) at N = 4k–65k [M]. Nearly all of it is encoder time.

### (c) Write path

```text
ALGORITHM W  WRITE(item)                    # after the answer or on capture; never on the read critical path
 1  e <- E(text); k <- unit(A e); store leaf {text, e, k, k0 = k, time} through ObjectStore (one transaction)
 2  PLACE: descend with the write bridge (unit(W e) · p_u), at each level choosing the best child with free slots;
    if the best score < theta_new or every slot is full: queue a "new parent" proposal for tonight (D.8)
    and attach temporarily to the best parent
 3  BM25 / FTS5 insert
 4  for each ancestor v, bottom-up: p_v <- P_theta(children) using cached child K/V; h_v <- H(...);
    gist_stale[v] <- (h_v != h_v^gist)                    # place + ancestors + flags: 0.34-0.51 ms [M]
 5  gists are NOT regenerated now (lazy). A reader that opens a stale gist whose ||p_v - t_v|| > delta
    descends to its children instead of trusting it; nightly D.7 re-distils
```

Measured total: **36–39 ms** including the encoder; **0.34–0.51 ms** without it; BM25 add/remove **0.15 ms** at 1e4 [M].

### (d) Forget path

```text
ALGORITHM F  FORGET(target)                 # synchronous part must finish before the next read
 1  resolve targets: a leaf, or every descendant of a parent, or every leaf matching a predicate
 2  delete content and per-node derived state: text, e_v, k_v, k0_v, drift, lateral links, FTS5/BM25 postings;
    remove from the ANN index (tombstone; full rebuild tonight)
 3  ancestors bottom-up: recompute p_v without the leaf; every ancestor gist that summarised it is blanked
    immediately (a gist may quote the deleted text) and queued for re-distillation before the next read uses it
 4  logs: delete learning-log entries whose O or C contain the target (keep a node -> entries index so this is
    a lookup, not a scan); drop it from replay and guard buffers; invalidate any cached LLM context containing it
 5  learned weights: heads refitted on logs that held the target still carry a trace -> mark tainted; next
    nightly refit restarts from theta_ship on the purged log (exact unlearning by retraining; costs seconds)
 6  storage: SQLite secure_delete; redact op-log rows; VACUUM tonight
 7  verify: search every store for the target's content hash and id -> must return zero hits
```

Measured synchronous part: **12–17 ms** [M]. Almost all of it is the naive scan over a 1e4-entry log; with the step-4 index it becomes sub-millisecond [X]. Re-distilling an affected gist is an LLM call, roughly 1–3 s per ancestor on device [derived from E].

## 3. Latency

### 3.1 Cost model

$$T_\text{hop}=T_\text{enc}(n_\text{tok})+T_\text{head}+T_\text{upper}+T_\text{leaf}(N)+T_\text{bm25}(N)+T_\text{fuse}+T_\text{fetch}$$
$$T_\text{ask}=\underbrace{T^{(1)}_\text{hop}}_{\text{prefetched}}+T_\text{TTFT}+\sum_{h=2}^{H}\big(T_\text{LLM-hop}+T^{(h)}_\text{hop}\big)+T_\text{gen}\qquad(\text{writes, updates and consolidation are off the critical path})$$

Scaling measured here: an exact fp32 scan costs about 1.2e-4 ms per key (1e6 keys = 118 ms, about 13 GB/s, memory-bound). An int8 scan costs about 3.6e-5 ms per key.

**How these numbers convert.** All [M] numbers are one x86 thread under Python. Sub-millisecond rows are dominated by interpreter overhead (5–20 µs per call), so they shrink in Swift with Accelerate. The scan rows are memory-bound and should carry over to Apple Silicon P-cores within roughly 0.5–2x [X]. The encoder is the row that moves the most: on the ANE with fixed shapes, Apple reports that latency stays roughly flat across short sequence lengths (32–128) for ANE-optimised transformers [E], and the [X] range assumes a several-fold gain. Measurement noise: the host is shared. b3, b4, b5 and b6 ran while a single-thread HNSW build occupied another core. A repeated 1e5 fp32 scan read 7 ms in one run and 10–13 ms in another, so treat ±50% as the noise band for memory-bound rows. A 4-thread encoder run was oversubscribed (about 1 s per ask) and was discarded. The known figure of about 6 ms per turn on 4 cores is consistent with 21 ms on one thread.

## 4. Performance plan (ranked)

1. **Move the encoder to the ANE and off the critical path.** It is at least 95% of a hop (26 ms of 25–36 ms) [M]. Convert bge-small to Core ML fp16 with fixed shapes 16/32/64/128, keep it resident, and pre-warm at launch. Encode the ask while the request is being assembled. Expected: several-fold faster [X]. **Do not** ship naive dynamic int8: it measured cosine 0.970 and top-10 overlap 0.73 against fp32. bf16 was identical to fp32 and 3x faster batched, but not faster for a single ask.
2. **Cut LLM-driven hops and overlap memory with LLM work.** Each LLM hop costs about one time to first token (0.35 s to over 10 s [E]), versus milliseconds for memory. Do this four ways:
   - Always run hop 1 before the first LLM call.
   - Prefetch hop-2 candidates with memory-only re-entry and lateral links while the LLM streams (speculative reads).
   - Let one tool call carry several read queries.
   - On Claude, use low effort, a cached stable prefix (system prompt, tools, root gist) with a max_tokens 0 pre-warm, and the "begin your visible answer immediately" instruction on routes where time to first token is visible.
3. **Fix the O(N log N) and Python-loop hot spots in the research code** (pure code fixes, measured):
   - BM25 scoring loop → postings: 6.5 ms to 0.04 ms at 1e4.
   - Full argsort → argpartition: 8.8 ms to 0.18 ms at 1e5.
   - RRF over full lists → top-50 lists: 7.4 ms to 0.024 ms.
   - On iPhone, use SQLite FTS5 `bm25()` through GRDB rather than a custom index.
4. **Cache action vectors and child K/V; recompute them only after a refit.** A read is then one scan. Path recompute with the cache is 0.3 ms, versus 1.2–1.7 ms without. Re-key costs 14 ms per 1e4 keys; do it in place to avoid the allocation blow-up at 1e5 (0.3 s now). CLM's 16.5 ms decision figure also relies on cached action vectors.
5. **Quantise stored keys to int8 above about 5e4 leaves, with an fp32 re-rank of the top 100.** Scans get 3.3–3.7x faster, memory drops 4x, and raw overlap is 0.95–0.97 [M]. Skip 1-bit codes: overlap fell to 0.76 at 1e5 with a 200-item re-rank pool.
6. **Batch the read, stop and multi-query decisions into one pass over the keys.** With int8, four queries cost about the same as one (2.45 vs 2.28 ms at 1e5). With fp32, 16 queries cost 1.85 ms per query versus about 10 ms alone [M]. The stop head reuses scores already computed.
7. **Use pyramid beam pruning only after trained parents pass F_B ≥ 0.95.** Mean-pooled parents keep 0.52–0.56 of the exact top-10 at B=8 and 0.85–0.94 at B=64 [M]. Below N_flat, the pyramid chooses granularity and does not prune.
8. **Add an ANN index (HNSW) only above about 2–3e5 leaves**, when the exact int8 scan exceeds about 5 ms on device. At 1e6 it measured 0.22–0.41 ms (overlap 0.84–0.92) versus 36 ms exact [M]. The catch is that every nightly re-key changes all keys, which forces a rebuild: 37 s at 1e5 and 501 s at 1e6 on one thread. Either index frozen base keys and apply learned keys as a re-rank, or rebuild inside the nightly window. At an assumed 50–100 items per day, a personal store reaches about 1e5–2e5 leaves in five years, so the flat path holds for years.
9. **Recompute parents incrementally with Merkle flags**, and chunk the whole-tree recompute by subtree. The 1e6 case (28 s) is allocation-bound: 35x the 1e5 time for 10x the data.
10. **Core ML/ANE for the heads and the internode encoder: not on the read path.** The heads take 6 µs, and ANE dispatch would cost more. It could help only the nightly whole-tree batch.
11. **One fused pass for BM25 and dense: no.** BM25 is already 0.04–0.34 ms.

**Do not optimise yet:**
- ANN indexes or IVF/PQ at personal scale.
- GPU or ANE for scans and heads.
- Fused kernels.
- 1-bit codes.
- An int8 encoder without calibration and a recall check.
- Multithreading the memory plane.
- Nightly training speed (seconds).
- Stage-3 in-model read serving, until stages 1–2 show quality gains on held-out benchmarks.

Spend the effort on hop policy, encoder placement, and descent fidelity, which is a quality problem rather than a speed problem.

issues: REPRODUCTION: 44 of the 54 listed medians fall within 30% (all scripts rerun sequentially with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 on an idle 4-core VM; side checks overlapped only the 1e6 HNSW build). Over all 188 raw rows, 49 fall outside 30%, and 36 of those take under 1 ms (Python-overhead noise). Every overlap and fidelity value reproduces exactly. The original 1e3-key rows in b2 read about 3x high, probably from contention.

NOT ROBUST: 'With int8, four queries cost about the same as one (2.45 vs 2.28 ms at 1e5)'. The rerun gave Q=4 4.49 ms vs Q=1 1.86 ms. A 3x repeat gave Q=1 1.7-3.3 ms and Q=4 2.5-3.4 ms. At 1e6, Q=4 costs 63 ms vs 34 ms for Q=1. Say instead: 'int8 per-query cost falls about 2x at Q=4 and 4-5x at Q=16'.

BATCH-VS-SINGLE BASELINE (perf item 6): '1.85 ms per query versus about 10 ms alone' compares against the GEMM-shaped Q=1 call in b2b. The right single-query baseline is the b2 GEMV, 6.8-7.1 ms, so the gain is about 4x, not 5x. Also, fp32 numpy at Q=4 gains nothing (24.6-27 ms vs 4 x 6.8 ms).

HOT-CACHE BIAS: this VM reports a 260 MiB L3, and each timing loop re-scans the same K. So the 1e4 (15 MB) and 1e5 (154 MB) fp32 scans run cache-resident. With a 768 MB sweep before each scan they measure 1.32 ms at 1e4 (0.60 hot) and 12.4 ms at 1e5 (7.3 hot). iPhone caches are far smaller, so project from the cold numbers. The '13 GB/s memory-bound' argument holds only for the 1e6 row.

WRONG HEADLINE: 'The encoder is at least 95% of a memory hop.' Under Algorithm R, flat leaf scoring is the default until F_B >= 0.95. On that path the encoder is 86% of the hop at 65k (39.7 ms total, 5.5 ms memory) and about 67% at 1e5 fp32 with a cold cache. 95% or more holds only for the pyramid path or N <= ~1e4. Quote the hop as 25-40 ms (flat).

Algorithm R annotation '1.9 ms int8 at 1e5' times only the int8 GEMM. The path R actually specifies (int8 scan + argpartition top-100 + fp32 rerank) measures 2.27 ms at 1e5 and 0.40 ms at 1e4, with top-10 overlap 1.000. The raw 0.95-0.97 overlap in item 5 therefore understates fidelity. Quote the post-rerank numbers.

SINGLE COLD RUNS: the b5 1e6 whole-tree run (warmup=0, n=1), the HNSW builds and the E5 fold are single runs. The 1e6 whole tree measured 19.0 s in the rerun vs 28.4 s, and 9.7 s when chunked by 65536-leaf subtrees. Allocation-bound is confirmed in direction, but '35x the 1e5 time for 10x' is not stable (the rerun gives 20x). Chunking measured 2-3x faster.

LABEL ERRORS: the b7 'read hop minus encoder (... + context)' row excludes the state head and the context fetch. 'Refit ~8-12 s [M]' (D step 3) and '8.4/11.5 s per 1e4 asks x 5 epochs' are extrapolated from 50 steps, so they are [X]. 'With the step-4 index it becomes sub-millisecond [X]' can now be [M]: the naive purge takes 11.3 ms of the 12.6-13.2 ms forget, and an index lookup takes 0.5 us.

SYNTHETIC KEYS UNDERSTATE DESCENT FIDELITY (finding 2): a k-means tree over REAL LoCoMo turn vectors (N=4096) keeps 0.82 at B=8, 0.96 at B=32 and 0.99 at B=64, vs 0.56/0.84/0.94 on synthetic keys. Within one persona (N=512, F=8, depth 3, that chat's own asks), B=8 keeps 0.74 (range 0.70-0.78) vs 0.57 synthetic. The conclusion holds (untrained parents miss 0.95 at small B), but 'loses most of the exact top-10' is too pessimistic. Label the synthetic-key caveat.

NOT A PURE CODE FIX: RRF over top-50 lists gives a different ranking from the full-list RRF used for the E1/E5/E6 recall numbers. Re-measure recall@10 before calling it speed-only. (The BM25 postings replacement is equivalent: top-10 agreement 0.988, ties only.)

ALGORITHM C EVIDENCE MISATTRIBUTED: +0.020 [0.014, 0.027] and the -0.003/-0.023/-0.023 figures come from the UNFILTERED move rule, with oracle cites, scored dense-only. Under C's own step 2 (cites restricted to opened nodes, the 'visible' condition in fix-cite-noise), move gives -0.002 [-0.007, +0.003]. Fused with BM25, as READ does, the oracle-cite gain is only +0.005. The 's.k >= 0.2 OR BM25 rank <= 10' filter was never evaluated. agree-bm25 alone cut the clean gain to +0.004.

ALGORITHM C FILTER IS VACUOUS: with bridged rank-16 heads on held-out chats, s.k >= 0.2 holds for 99.97% of opened top-10 nodes (p1 = 0.244) and 90% of gold. It is the system's own score, not an independent signal. Because step 2 already restricts cites to opened nodes, step 4 removes nothing. Replace it with a rule that was measured under visible cites: contrastive gave +0.008 [0.004, 0.013], and +0.014 at 30% wrong cites. Note also that capping at the '3 best by s.k' favours nodes that already rank high.
LOGGING BUG (C step 7 -> D step 3): the log stores s = unit(S x), but refitting S needs the pre-head x = E(q). Log x, and treat it as user data under FORGET.
D STEP 3 NEGATIVES: 'hard negatives O \ C'' include genuine cites that C's cap or filter removed, so they get trained as negatives. Use O \ C (raw cites).

D GATE CANNOT SEE IMPROVEMENT AND IS LEAKY: (1) T_eval positives are cites, and C makes those a subset of theta_cur's own top-10, so theta_cur scores about 1 by construction. Any reordering can only lose, which means the gate measures agreement with theta_cur. (2) The refit early-stops on T_eval and is then gated on T_eval (selection bias). (3) Online drift was learned from T_eval's own cites, so drift-keyed evaluation leaks labels. Step 5's 'keep drift only if replay says it helps' tests drift on its own training data. Fix: split fit/select/gate by time; gate both arms on anchor keys k0; log the top-50 candidates with ranks so gains can show up (recall@50, MRR); judge gains on G and by interleaving; evaluate drift prequentially from scores logged at ask time.

D RATCHET: a non-inferiority margin of eps = 0.005 per night, measured against theta_cur, compounds over many nights. Also require no loss against a fixed floor (theta_ship on G plus a frozen user eval set).

D UNGATED STEPS: step 7 re-distils gists with no faithfulness check, and those gists are shown to R and used as fallback keys. Step 8's structure gate is vacuous while READ uses flat leaf scoring (leaf recall unchanged, so it 'does not drop'), and many proposals tested on one T_eval invites a winner's curse. Step 5 RE-KEY lacks unit() and adds drift computed in the old key space to the new one.

CONSOLIDATION RACE: D snapshots V_t and later commits V_{t+1} atomically. Writes and forgets that arrive during consolidation are lost at commit, and forgotten items come back. Journal every W/F operation since the snapshot and replay it onto V_{t+1} before commit. The retained rollback copy V_t must also get the forgets.
